newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Tuesday:
* On Monday, the Dow Jones ended at 6,709.18 points, up 5.39 points. PLDT's ADR rose by $0 1/8 at $56 5/8.
* On Monday, the peso closed at 26.327 to a U.S. dollar from 26.337.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed at 3,270.31 up 8.17.
* The Philippine interbank call loan rate was unchanged at 10.53125 pct.
* The yield on the benchmark 91-day Treasury bill plunges to a 14-month low of 10.746 percent, shedding 42.6 basis points from 11.172 percent last week. (TODAY, MANILA TIMES)

* The Philippine government is likely to meet all of the five performance criteria set under the three-year Extended Fund Facility programme sponsored by the International Monetary Fund. (CHRONICLE/PHILIPPINE STAR/BULLETIN)

* A Multisectoral task force on power wants government to defer the full deregulation of the oil industry which is set on or before March 1997 until the energy department resolves four pressing issues which includes the 2.4 billion pesos unsettled claims of local oil refiners. (INQUIRER/MALAYA)

* Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc buys majority control of Pepsi Cola Products Philippines Inc (PCPPI) through the purchase of the shares of Macondray Holdings Corp, Belle Corp, Comtrust Holdings Inc and Transnational Diversified Corp in Premier Beverages Philippines Inc. Premier owns 51.5 percent of the capital stock of PCPPI. (TIMES JOURNAL/INQUIRER)
* The Energy Regulatory Board is set to announce another round of oil price adjustments on Friday with liquefied petroleum gasoline raised the most by 89 centavos per litre. (BUSINESSWORLD)
